_note: TNFD 'Locate' screening for a single building, island-wide. Each test is a threshold on a measured distance or value. 'basis' says whether the threshold comes from a Singapore rule ('cited') or is a HELIOS screening choice ('method') — method thresholds are flags for a closer look, not findings of harm.

framework.name: TNFD LEAP approach — Locate phase (interface with nature, sensitive locations)

tests.label: Inside a nature reserve or national park
tests.source: URA Master Plan 2025 SDCP Nature Reserve, National Park and Nature Area Boundary; reserves are protected under the Parks and Trees Act 2005

tests.label: Within 500 m of a nature reserve or national park
tests.source: HELIOS screening buffer — edge effects (light, noise, run-off) reach a few hundred metres; NParks may ask for an environmental study near reserves

tests.label: Within 100 m of a designated nature area
tests.source: HELIOS screening buffer around URA MP2025 Nature Areas

tests.label: Within 250 m of mangrove, seagrass, coral or mudflat
tests.source: NParks Coastal and Marine Habitat Map 2018; HELIOS screening buffer

tests.label: Ground below 3 m above mean sea level
tests.source: PUB: before 2011 the minimum platform level for new developments was 3 m above mean sea level; raised to at least 4 m in 2011. Mean sea level may rise up to 1.15 m by 2100 (NCCS, V3).

tests.label: Ground below today's 4 m minimum platform level
tests.source: PUB: minimum platform level for new developments raised to at least 4 m above mean sea level since 2011

tests.label: Within 300 m of a PUB flood-prone location
tests.source: PUB List of Flood Prone Areas (Nov 2025); 300 m is a HELIOS buffer around each geocoded location

tests.label: Less than 10% vegetation within 100 m
tests.source: ESA WorldCover 2021. Low surrounding greenery is associated with higher surface and air temperatures; 10% is a HELIOS screening cut, not a standard.

caveats: Ground level is estimated from a 30 m surface model (Copernicus DEM, includes roofs and trees) by taking the 10th percentile of non-water cells within ~75 m. Expect ±2–4 m; a survey platform level always wins.
Flood-prone locations are PUB's named streets geocoded to one point each; PUB does not publish their extents.
GBIF records reflect where people look as much as where species live (observer bias), so species counts compare areas loosely.
IUCN threatened categories come via GBIF from the IUCN Red List, which is free for non-commercial use only. Commercial use would need an IUCN/IBAT licence.
